Computational Complexity Theory

  • Instructors : Chandan Saha   Course number and Credits : E0 224 and 3:1   Lecture time : M,W 2-3:30 pm   Venue : CSA 112

  • Syllabus :
    • P, NP and NP-completeness
    • Space complexity
    • Polynomial time hierarchy
    • Boolean circuits
    • Randomized computation
    • Complexity of counting

  • References :
    1. Computational Complexity - A Modern Approach by Sanjeev Arora and Boaz Barak
      2. (We'll closely follow this book)
    2. Computational Complexity Theory by Steven Rudich and Avi Wigderson (Editors)
    3. Mathematics and Computation by Avi Wigderson
    4. Boolean Function Complexity by Stasys Jukna
    5. Gems of Theoretical Computer Science by Schoening and Pruim
    6. The Nature of Computation by Moore and Mertens
    7. The Complexity Theory Companion by Hemaspaandra and Ogihara
    8. Online lecture notes... (take a look at this webpage)

  • Prerequisites : Familiarity with undergraduate level data structures & algorithms, and some mathematical maturity.

  • Grading policy :
    • Assignments - 45%
    • Presentation - 25%
    • Final exam - 30%

  • Assignments :
    • Assignment 1 (due date: Sep 18, 2022)
    • Assignment 2 (due date: Oct 19, 2022)
    • Assignment 3 (due date: Nov 23, 2022)

  • Final exam : Dec 6 (Tuesday), 10 am -- 1 pm in CSA 112

  • Lectures :
    • Lecture 1: Introduction; Turing machines
    • Lecture 2: Class P & NP; Karp reductions; NP-completeness
    • Lecture 3: Cook-Levin theorem
    • Lecture 4: Cook-Levin theorem (contd.)
    • Lecture 5: More NP-complete problems; Search versus Decision
    • Lecture 6: NTMs; Class co-NP and EXP
    • Lecture 7: Time Hierarchy Theorem; Ladner's Theorem
    • Lecture 8: Ladner's theorem (contd.); Relativization
    • Lecture 9: Space complexity classes
    • Lecture 10: Savitch's theorem; PSPACE-completeness; Log-space reductions
    • Lecture 11: NL-completeness; NL = co-NL
    • Lecture 12: Polynomial Hierarchy
    • Lecture 13: Polynomial Hierarchy (contd.); Boolean circuits; Class P/poly
    • Lecture 14: Karp-Lipton theorem; Classes NC and AC
    • Lecture 15: P-completeness; Parity not in AC0
    • Lecture 16: Parity not in AC0 (contd.): The Switching Lemma
    • Lecture 17: Probabilistic Turing machines; Class BPP
    • Lecture 18: Sipser-Gacs-Lautemann theorem; Classes RP, co-RP and ZPP; Bipartite matching in RNC
    • Lecture 19-20: Class BPL; Randomized reductions; GNI is in BP.NP
    • Lecture 21: Complexity of Counting
    • Lecture 22-23: 0/1-Permanent is #P-complete
    • Lecture 24: Class PP and ⊕P; Valiant-Vazirani theorem
    • Lecture 25: Toda's theorem: Randomized reduction from PH to ⊕SAT
    • Lecture 26: Toda's theorem: Deterministic reduction from PH to #SAT

  • Student presentations :
    • Deterministic primality testing
    • Interactive_proofs
    • Parallel complexity of the determinant
    • UPATH is in L
    • Parallel algorithms for matching
